title: Slocum Road Trail Cameras
description: Forty clips off six trail cameras on sixty acres at Coyne Flats: deer, raccoons, a culvert, one animal that is probably a dog, and a great deal of nothing at three in the morning.

channels.name: Cam 1 - woodlot, north corner
channels.about:
Strapped to a shagbark on the north corner of the woodlot, eleven feet in from the bean field, pointed at the gap in the hedge where the deer have always come through.

This is the busiest of the six and about a third of what is on this page came off it. Card out Sunday mornings.

The gap is not mine and neither is the hedge. It is Ellen Sowder's hedge and she knows the camera is there.

channels.name: Cam 2 - Coyne Creek
channels.about:
On a locust post in Ellen Sowder's field on the Coyne Flats side, about forty feet back from the county's fence and pointed at the Coyne Creek trestle. With her permission, in writing, because I asked for it in writing.

I do not put cameras on county land and I am not going to start.

The structure itself is roughly two hundred feet off, which is four times what one of these cameras will ever detect, so this one runs a frame a minute for forty minutes at first light and last light and motion the rest of the time. That is why half of what is here is grass and the other half is four minutes long.

What happens to the bridge is not my business and there is a whole board for it: [url=synth://trailusers.verity.net/topic/tt-04]Coyne Creek trestle - deck it like the other three[/url]. If you want to know who to write to about the corridor, it is [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/rail-crossing]Rail Crossing and Right-of-Way Inquiries[/url], which is the wrong-looking page and the right department.

channels.name: Cam 3 - Dry Fork culvert
channels.about:
Low on a steel post at the mouth of the stone culvert that takes the Dry Fork under the old rail grade, about a hundred yards on the Coyne Flats side of the mile 9 marker.

Everything short and wet in this county goes through that culvert. The camera sits eighteen inches off the ground, which is the right height for a mink and the wrong height for anything else, and is why a good many of these are the back end of something leaving.

channels.name: Cam 4 - Hauk orchard
channels.about:
Eleven apple trees and a fallen-in springhouse on the old Hauk place, the other side of the lane.

Nobody has lived there since 2011 and the family is in another state, so I wrote to the daughter and she wrote back and said help yourself and send me one of the deer ones at Christmas. I have sent her four.

Windfalls start the third week of September and then everything in the county comes through in about nine days.

channels.name: Cam 5 - back of the house
channels.about:
Screwed to the porch rail, four feet up, looking at the ground under the feeder.

Raccoons, a possum, a skunk that has never once been in a hurry, and a grey cat that belongs to nobody and eats here anyway.

Joyce checks this one before she checks the weather.

channels.name: Cam 6 - gate, Slocum Road
channels.about:
On the gate post at the end of the lane, pointed up the lane.

It is there so I know who turned in, and the answer is nearly always the propane truck. I leave the dull ones up because the dull ones are the honest ones and because taking them down would mean deciding which ones are dull.

channels.name: Setup, tests and dead cards
channels.about:
Wes Lankford, Slocum Road, Coyne Flats. Sixty acres, six cameras, and a notebook that goes back to the spring of 2025.

Six cameras, all the cheap no-glow kind, four of them the same model. Eight AA cells each, which gets me about seven weeks in summer and four in January. 32 gigabyte cards, swapped Sunday mornings on a loop round the place that takes an hour and ten minutes and is the best part of my week.

Settings are the same on all six except Cam 2: twenty second video, thirty second delay, sensitivity medium. High sensitivity gets you nine hundred clips of grass and a flat battery by Thursday.

The cameras are [url=synth://gridfalldeals.com/p/p-17]the forty-six dollar ones[/url]. They are fine. The hundred and twenty foot detection range is not a hundred and twenty feet, it is about fifty-five, and nobody who has ever hung one on a tree would tell you otherwise.

Cards from [url=synth://dellshardware.synth/]Dell's in Coyne Flats[/url], six dollars each, and I have never had one of theirs fail. Their website has said coming soon since about 2015.

This page is an old gallery script a fellow in Gridfall set up for me in 2019 for forty dollars and a pie. It does not do playlists, it does not do folders, and it will not let me delete a comment. The only way I know to hold a clip at the top of the front page is to put it in first, which is why the fog one says March and sits above things from September.

It also calls itself an archive and prints [i]video files were not preserved[/i] at the bottom of every page, which is not true, because the files are right here. I have never worked out how to change that line and neither has anybody I have asked.

People ask me what I am looking for out there. Nothing. I like knowing what walks through.

items.title: 2026-03-08 05:40 - Cam 2 Coyne Creek trestle
items.description: Time-lapse, one frame a minute, 05:40 to 06:20. Fog off the creek and then no fog. Nothing crosses it, because there is nothing to cross on. This one stays at the top.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: I ride out to that fence most weeks and I have never once seen it do this. Thank you for getting up.

comments.author: wardlow
comments.body:
Twelve years I have photographed that structure from the trail side and I did not know the fog sat on it like that.

I would like the still at about two minutes if you can get one off the card.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: The frame you want is 05:59. I will put it on a card and leave it in your box, I go past on Thursdays.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body:
There is a heron in exactly one frame, at 1:12, on the near bar. Great blue, not a crane. We do not have cranes here and we are not going to have them because somebody wrote crane on a video.

If anybody wants to argue about it there is a place for that: [url=synth://veritybirders.org/board/b-id]Identification Help[/url].

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: The locust post your camera is screwed to has a rub on it at about chest height on a deer, and it is fresh. Whatever you are pointing that thing at, something is using the post.

comments.author: c_pruitt
comments.body:
The stone you can see at the near end from 2:05 is the abutment, and it is the only part of the whole structure the 2013 assessment calls sound. Everything above it is the part with the problem.

The dimensions are on the wiki if anyone wants them without reading eighty-four pages: [url=synth://verity.wiki/wiki/verity-branch-trail]Verity Branch Trail[/url].

comments.author: VerityPulseAI
comments.body:
This footage shows the historic Coyne Creek trestle, a well-known landmark on the Verity Branch Trail which has been closed to the public since 2016. Residents have expressed a range of views about the structure over the years, and local officials have not commented.

Why not share your own trail memories with the community today?

items.title: 2025-10-19 02:41 - Cam 4 Hauk orchard
items.description: A large dark animal at the back of the orchard, right at the edge of what the infrared reaches. I do not know what it is.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body:
It is a dog.

Look at the tail at eleven seconds. It comes up and over the back and it stays there. A bear cannot do that, because a bear has not got one worth speaking of. The gait is a trot and it is a dog's trot, front foot and opposite back foot together, and you can count it.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: The shoulder still looks wrong to me for a dog.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: The shoulder is wrong for a dog six feet away. That animal is forty feet away, at night, through two apple trees, on a sensor the size of a pea. Everything is wrong for everything at forty feet.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: There is a black Newfoundland cross that lives at the Ashkettle end of Slocum Road and gets out about twice a month. Its name is Barrow and it is somewhere around a hundred and thirty pounds.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: That is probably the end of it, then.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: The low pair of eyes to the right at 0:04 is a possum, for whatever that is worth to anybody.

comments.author: AutoLocal_Feed
comments.body:
Residents are reminded that black bear sightings should be reported to the county and that bear activity in the region has increased in recent years, although sightings remain uncommon. Experts advise securing food sources and keeping a safe distance at all times.

Stay safe and stay informed this season.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body:
Somebody put this on [url=synth://gridline.social/]Gridline[/url] with the title BEAR SPOTTED IN VERITY COUNTY and it did about four hundred points. I have had nine emails, two of them from out of state, and a man rang the house.

It is a dog. I am leaving the clip up because it is what the camera got, and I am leaving this comment under it because that is the only correction I am able to make.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: It is a dog.

items.title: 2026-06-21 05:52 - Cam 1 woodlot
items.description: Doe and two fawns through the hedge gap, unhurried, in that order.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Both fawns still well spotted on the twenty-first of June puts them at about six weeks, which means she dropped them in the second week of May. That is on time for here and it always has been, whatever anybody tells you about the seasons moving.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: The one at the back is smaller by a third. Worth watching for on the later cards.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: Both of them are on the twelfth of July clip and the little one has caught up some.

items.title: 2026-08-09 23:18 - Cam 5 back of the house
items.description: Four raccoons on the porch rail at once, which is the record.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: Three of those are this year's. The one that stays on the post and does not eat is the sow.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Count again at 0:21. There are four kits, not three, and the fourth is behind the post with only a foot showing. So five animals.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: That feeder is going to come down.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: It came down at twelve minutes past four the next morning. That is the following clip.

items.title: 2026-07-12 06:03 - Cam 1 woodlot
items.description: Same doe, both fawns, spots going on the bigger one.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Nine weeks, near enough. The spots go from the back forward and that is what you are seeing.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: The small one is still small but it is keeping up, which is the part that matters.

items.title: 2025-11-02 03:17 - Cam 1 woodlot
items.description: Buck working the branch over the gap. He is back at 03:44 on the same card and does the same thing again.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Count the points again. The brow tine on his left is snapped off about an inch up, so he is a seven on the ground and an eight if you are feeling generous, and most people are feeling generous in November.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: Seven, then.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: The tree he is working is an ash and it has been dead two years. It will be on the ground inside another two and it will take your camera with it. [url=synth://verityextension.org/post/road-frontage-ash]The extension office has been saying this about every ash in the county[/url] and nobody wants to hear it about their own.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Move the camera and keep the tree. He is coming for the branch, not for the shagbark.

items.title: 2026-01-18 03:02 - Cam 1 woodlot
items.description: Nothing. Snow coming down hard enough to set the camera off on its own.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Ten seconds of snow falling in the dark is still the nicest thing I have watched this week and I am not going to pretend otherwise.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Wet snow does it every time. Each flake is warmer than the air behind it as far as the sensor is concerned.

items.title: 2026-02-15 03:41 - Cam 1 woodlot
items.description: Coyote, one, left to right, not stopping for anything.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Coyote. The tail is down and straight and it stays down and straight, which is the thing to look at before you look at anything else. A dog carries it up. A dog also looks at the camera and this one did not.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: That is the same animal as the one on Cam 3 from the ninth. The white on the chest is the same shape and it is off centre the same way.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: Six days and about a mile and a half apart. I would not have put those two together.

items.title: 2025-09-28 04:55 - Cam 1 woodlot
items.description: Turkeys, eleven of them, in no order at all.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: Eleven is right, and there are two broods in there rather than one. Hens at 0:03 and at 0:19, and the poults are about a month apart in size, which you can see best when the two groups overlap at 0:26.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: I counted nine the first time and ten the second.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Everybody counts nine the first time.

items.title: 2026-05-10 03:33 - Cam 1 woodlot
items.description: Nothing at all for the whole clip. There is a leaf on the lens and it is the leaf that is moving.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: There is something on the right at 0:14.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: That is the leaf. It is two inches from the glass so it looks like it is forty feet away and the size of a dog.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Half of every trail camera argument in this county is something two inches from the glass.

items.title: 2026-09-13 06:40 - Cam 1 woodlot
items.description: Doe standing in the gap for the whole two minutes doing nothing whatever.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Ears forward the entire time and she never once turns her head. She was listening to the camera, not to you. They hear the focus motor on these.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: Whatever is calling at 1:31 is a blue jay. Your camera does record sound, which I had assumed it did not.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body:
So had I, for four years.

Power was off here from Saturday evening until about four on Sunday morning and the cameras did not care, which is one of the few advantages they have over everything else in this house. Somebody logged the outage properly: [url=synth://scanner.verity.net/post/log-2026-09-12]Sat 12 Sep 2026 into Sun 13 Sep[/url].

items.title: 2025-05-04 19:22 - Cam 2 Coyne Creek
items.description: Fox up onto the near abutment, along it, and off the other side.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Red fox, and thin through the flank, which in the first week of May means she is feeding a litter and has been for a while.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: There is an earth in the bank forty yards up on the trail side. You can see the spoil from the fence if you know to look for it, and now everybody does, so leave it alone.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: Phoebe on the fence wire at 0:06, which is not interesting to anybody but me.

items.title: 2025-12-21 03:09 - Cam 2 Coyne Creek
items.description: Nothing. Twenty seconds of the fence and the frost on it.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: The shortest day and twenty seconds of a fence. It is exactly right.

items.title: 2026-07-05 04:48 - Cam 2 Coyne Creek
items.description: Time-lapse at first light. Three deer on the far bank, and then the same three on the near bank, and the bridge has nothing to do with it.

comments.author: c_pruitt
comments.body: They are using the ford about eighty yards downstream, where the bank breaks down on both sides. They have used it for as long as anybody has been here and the railway did not ask them either.

comments.author: wardlow
comments.body: I have looked at this eight times. I am not going to say the thing I usually say.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: He did not say it.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Two does and a yearling. The yearling goes in last and comes out first, which is the whole of being a yearling.

items.title: 2026-02-22 16:10 - Cam 2 Coyne Creek
items.description: Ice most of the way across the creek and a mink working the open edge of it.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Mink. Long body, short legs, and it never once stops moving, which is the tell. A muskrat swims like it has somewhere to be. A mink swims like it has forgotten where that was.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: Kingfisher on the dead limb at 0:09 and it is still there at 0:18. They stay all winter if there is open water, and that is open water.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Two animals in twenty seconds in February is a good card.

items.title: 2025-08-24 21:05 - Cam 2 Coyne Creek
items.description: Barred owl on the near cap. It was there eleven minutes and the camera gave me forty seconds of it.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: Barred owl. You can hear it once at 0:26 and it is the two-note contact call, not the eight-note one everybody knows. Pairs do that back and forth for an hour and it carries a long way up a creek.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Eleven minutes and you got forty seconds, which is the whole problem with these cameras in one line.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body:
It is the whole problem with these cameras. Thirty second delay after every trigger, and an owl that is not moving does not trigger it again.

I could set the delay to nothing and get four hundred clips of the same owl and a flat battery on Tuesday. There is no setting that gives you eleven minutes of owl.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: There is. It is called going and sitting there.

items.title: 2026-02-09 04:31 - Cam 3 Dry Fork culvert
items.description: Coyote at the culvert mouth. Drinks, listens, goes.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Same animal you get on Cam 1 six days later. The chest patch is off centre to its left both times and the notch out of the right ear is in both clips.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: The ear is the better mark of the two. A chest patch changes shape with how the animal is standing and an ear does not.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: So there is one coyote working the whole grade rather than four of them, which is a nicer thought than the one I had.

items.title: 2025-06-15 02:20 - Cam 3 Dry Fork culvert
items.description: A mink, or the back half of one, for two seconds.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Mink. Out at 0:02, back in at 0:04, and that is about all anybody has ever got of one.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: Eighteen inches off the ground and I still only get the half that is leaving.

items.title: 2026-04-26 05:14 - Cam 3 Dry Fork culvert
items.description: Four inches of water over the sill and a wood duck standing in it looking put out.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: Wood duck, hen. They nest in the dead sycamore on the Sowder side and have done every year I have been counting, which is since 1998. She will have brought the brood down the Dry Fork and this is where they come out.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: The water is over the sill every April and back down by the second week of May. It has been doing that since long before the trail.

items.title: 2025-07-20 03:50 - Cam 3 Dry Fork culvert
items.description: Seven days on the card and one animal on it, and the animal is a moth two inches from the lens.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: How many triggers on the card?

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: Six hundred and forty-one. Six hundred and forty of them are the grass in front of the culvert and I have watched all of them, because you have to watch all of them to find out that they are the grass.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Cut the grass. I know you will not.

items.title: 2026-08-16 01:58 - Cam 3 Dry Fork culvert
items.description: Raccoon coming out of the culvert carrying something it did not want photographed.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Crayfish. You can see the claw against its chest at 0:11 and you can see the other one on the ground at 0:04, which it goes back for.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: The Dry Fork is full of them. The children used to bring them up in buckets and put them in the stock tank.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: It is the second-best clip on this site and I am not going to say which is the first.

items.title: 2026-09-06 04:22 - Cam 3 Dry Fork culvert
items.description: Nothing. The camera fired at twenty-two past four and there is nothing in the frame, and this happens at this camera all autumn.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Warm air coming out of the culvert across the cold stone at the mouth. The sensor reads a moving warm edge and there is nothing in front of it to read. Mine at the pond does it from about the first week of September until the frost settles it.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: That is the first explanation of it anybody has given me in four years and it took you one paragraph. I had a page of results about it once and every one of them said the same three things and none of them said that.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Ray has been doing this since before there were pages of results.

items.title: 2025-10-05 18:40 - Cam 3 Dry Fork culvert
items.description: Skunk in and out of the culvert four times in six minutes, on four separate clips, stitched.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Striped skunk, and there is a second one sitting on the bank at 0:30 that never moves. They do that. One works and one sits.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: Two.

comments.author: wildlife_cams_pro
comments.body: Great content!!! For BEST trail camera deals and honest reviews visit [url=synth://camera-deals-outlet.top/trail]camera-deals-outlet[/url] - free ship 48 state - 4K NO GLOW from $19

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: I cannot delete comments on this script. I can only stop reading them, and I have.

items.title: 2025-09-21 20:14 - Cam 4 Hauk orchard
items.description: Windfalls started on the Friday and by Sunday evening this is what forty seconds under one tree looks like.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Three deer, a raccoon and a groundhog inside forty seconds and all of them on the same eight apples, with about a yard between them and none of them bothered.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: That is the best forty seconds on this site.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: There are two more up the tree. Grey squirrels, top right, from 0:22, and they are the reason the apples are coming down at eight in the evening in the first place.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: I have watched this thirty times and I never saw the squirrels.

items.title: 2026-05-17 06:02 - Cam 4 Hauk orchard
items.description: Time-lapse at first light. The orchard in blossom with nothing in it.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Thank you.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: There are at least three bumblebee species working those trees at that hour and the camera cannot see one of them, which is fair enough. It was not built for bees.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Eleven trees and nine of them still setting fruit after however many years with nobody near them. Whoever put those in knew what they were doing.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: Hauk's grandfather, and the daughter says it was 1948 or thereabouts. She is not certain and neither am I, so take it as about then.

items.title: 2026-03-22 03:36 - Cam 4 Hauk orchard
items.description: Possum on the springhouse wall, going nowhere in particular and taking its time about it.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Possum. Bare tail, bare ears, and the ears are white at the edge and black at the base on this one. If you see it again you will know it.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: It is on the porch camera in December. Same ears.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: A possum crossing from the orchard to the house is about four hundred yards, which is nothing to them. They will go a mile and a half in a night and be back before light.

items.title: 2026-01-04 02:12 - Cam 4 Hauk orchard
items.description: Nothing but snow on the branches, and then one branch letting go of its snow.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: 0:17. That is the whole clip and I nearly did not keep it.

items.title: 2026-09-20 05:48 - Cam 4 Hauk orchard
items.description: First windfalls of this year and a doe already on them at ten to six in the morning.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Three days earlier than last year.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: Two. Last year's was the twenty-first and it was on the ground on the Friday, so it is two days, and I only know that because it is written on the same page in the same notebook.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Two days over a year is nothing at all and people will make a chart out of it anyway.

items.title: 2026-08-10 04:12 - Cam 5 back of the house
items.description: The feeder comes down.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: Eleven weeks that feeder lasted.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: Nine. I put it up on the seventh of June.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: The one that does it is the sow and she does it by weight, not by cleverness. She hangs on it until the hook opens. There is nothing to solve.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Clever enough.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: New hook, three dollars twenty at Dell's, and a length of chain off the barn. We will see how long that lasts.

items.title: 2025-11-09 21:40 - Cam 5 back of the house
items.description: The skunk. Same skunk, same twenty minutes either side of half past nine, all autumn.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Striped skunk, and it is the same one every time. The stripe splits high on the shoulder on this animal. The other one that comes round splits low, nearly at the hip, and if you get both on a card you will never mix them up again.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: It has never been in a hurry in its life and it does not have to be.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: It is eating the seed the jays throw down, which is most of the seed.

items.title: 2026-06-28 03:24 - Cam 5 back of the house
items.description: The grey cat, twenty seconds, and it knows exactly where the camera is.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: That cat has been on Slocum Road longer than I have been riding out here, and I started in 2016.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: If anybody is feeding it, the birds under that feeder would like to know.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: We are feeding it. It came with the cold snap in 2019 and it has not left and it will not come in the house.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: It looks at the lens at 0:11 and then walks out of frame on the side where there is no path. It has worked out the red glow is not nothing, and that is a cat that has been shot at.

items.title: 2026-01-25 04:44 - Cam 5 back of the house
items.description: Nothing. A quarter to five in the morning, minus eleven, and the camera fired anyway.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Batteries go strange at minus eleven and a strange battery fires the camera. Mine all do it in January and then stop doing it in March.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Lithiums, if you can stand paying for them.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: Six cameras, eight cells each. I have done that sum and I am not doing it again.

items.title: 2025-12-14 22:50 - Cam 5 back of the house
items.description: Possum eating what the raccoons left, which is nothing.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: It is on the seed the jays threw down. There is always seed on the ground and by December there is never any in the feeder, which tells you what a feeder is actually for.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Same ears as the orchard one.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Same possum. White edge, black base. It is a four hundred yard walk and it has all night.

items.title: 2026-09-14 04:12 - Cam 5 back of the house
items.description: A raccoon, the possum and the cat in the same twenty seconds, none of them interested in the others.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: This is the whole site in one clip.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Nothing here has ever been in a hurry and nothing here has ever had a reason to be.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: The cat is not hunting. It is waiting for the raccoon to leave, same as the possum is.

items.title: 2026-09-07 11:02 - Cam 6 gate, Slocum Road
items.description: The propane truck, which is what Cam 6 is mostly for.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: I have watched this twice.

comments.author: AutoLocal_Feed
comments.body:
Residents across Verity County have been sharing footage of local deliveries as household fuel costs continue to be a concern for many families in the region. Local officials say preparation is key ahead of the colder months.

What does your household do to prepare for winter? Let us know in the comments below.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: It is a propane truck.

items.title: 2025-08-31 14:25 - Cam 6 gate, Slocum Road
items.description: The mail carrier, and the dog that comes with her.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: That is a border collie cross and it is running the mail route better than the car is. It knows which boxes.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Her name is Cass and she has been on that route since Bev took it over.

items.title: 2026-03-01 12:18 - Cam 6 gate, Slocum Road
items.description: The plough, four days after it was any use to anybody.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Slocum is a level three road. Level three means after everything else, and everything else is a long list in a bad week.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body:
It always has been. I am not complaining, I am saying that is the plough and that is when it came.

I drove a fuel truck on these roads for thirty-one years and I would not have got down here any sooner.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Four days is not bad for the first of March.

items.title: 2026-06-14 21:33 - Cam 6 gate, Slocum Road
items.description: Somebody turning round in the lane, which happens about once a week from May to October.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Trail traffic. They miss the Coyne Flats lot, they get to the end of the made road, and the next place wide enough to turn a car is your gate.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: The lot is signed from the Ashkettle side and it is not signed from yours. It has never been signed from yours.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: I have stopped minding. They turn round, they wave, they go. Twice this year somebody has got out and asked for directions and both times I sent them the right way, which is more than the sign would have done.

items.title: 2025-04-13 13:05 - Cam 1 setup test
items.description: The first thing this camera ever recorded is my hand and the strap coming loose.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Leave it up.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: It is staying up. It is the only clip on here I am in.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Use the cam strap once to find the tree and then put a screw in it. The straps all go in about two winters and then the camera is on the ground pointing at the sky and you have four weeks of sky.

items.title: 2026-02-01 00:00 - Cam 3 card failure
items.description: A dead card looks like this: eleven days, one file, one second of grey. Kept because it is the only way I have of showing what those eleven days were.

comments.author: r_ostler
comments.body: Buy the cards in town. The cheap ones off the internet are the cheap ones off the internet, and the brand on the label is not the brand in the card.

comments.author: w_lankford
comments.body: [url=synth://dellshardware.synth/]Dell's in Coyne Flats[/url], six dollars, and I have never had one of theirs fail. Their page has said coming soon since about 2015 and Dell is not in a hurry either.

comments.author: dee_hollis
comments.body: Eleven days of nothing is still eleven days of something. You just have not got it.

comments.author: m_halvorsen
comments.body: That is the trouble with all of this and it is the trouble with the bird records as well. The count is not what happened. The count is what somebody was standing there to see.
